text:
Entry points at Year 7 (age 11), Year 9 (age 13), and Sixth Form (age 16).

**Year 7 entry:** The Beri Entrance Exam is held each January. The exam covers English, mathematics, and verbal reasoning. Shortlisted candidates are invited to interview in February. Places are confirmed by the end of February, with acceptance required within two weeks.

**Year 9 entry:** Candidates sit the ISEB Common Pre-Test in Year 6 or 7, followed by a school-specific assessment in English and mathematics. Interviews are held in the Lent term.

**Sixth Form entry:** A minimum of 6 GCSEs at grade 7 or above is required. Subject-specific interviews are held in November for the following September's intake. Conditional offers are made based on predicted GCSE grades.

Registration deadline: 31 October for all entry points. A non-refundable registration fee of £150 applies.

Open mornings are held in October and November each year. Private tours are available year-round by appointment through the Admissions Office.
title: Admissions

text:
Years 7–11: £7,200 per term (£21,600 per annum). Sixth Form (Years 12–13): £7,800 per term (£23,400 per annum).

Fees are reviewed each September; the current schedule is effective from September 2024. Lunch is included in the termly fee for all year groups.

Extras not included in fees: residential trips, individual music tuition (charged per term), and external examination entry fees.

Payment is due by the first day of each term. The school accepts direct debit (monthly or termly) and termly lump sum payments. A 2% discount is offered for annual payment in advance.

Sibling discount: a 5% reduction on the younger sibling's fees applies when two or more siblings attend concurrently.
title: Tuition Fees

text:
Academic scholarships are available at 11+, 13+, and 16+ entry points, offering up to 20% fee remission. Awards are made on the basis of entrance exam performance and interview.

Music scholarships offer up to 15% fee remission. An audition is required; instruments considered include piano, strings, voice, and brass. Candidates should normally have reached Grade 5 or above on their principal instrument.

Sport scholarships offer up to 10% fee remission. A trial is required; sports considered include rugby, swimming, and athletics. Candidates should demonstrate county-level or equivalent ability.

Means-tested bursaries are available up to 100% of fees for families with demonstrable financial need. Bursary applications are assessed independently and confidentially by the Bursar's office.

Scholarship applications close two weeks before the relevant entrance assessment. All awards are reviewed annually; holders must maintain academic and conduct standards to retain their award.
title: Scholarships

text:
**GCSE subjects (Years 10–11):** All pupils study English Language, English Literature, Mathematics, and the three sciences (Biology, Chemistry, Physics) as core subjects. Optional subjects are chosen from: History, Geography, French, German, Spanish, Religious Studies, Art & Design, Drama, Music, Computer Science, and Physical Education.

**A-Level subjects (Years 12–13):** Students typically choose three or four subjects from: Mathematics, Further Mathematics, English Literature, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, History, Geography, French, German, Spanish, Economics, Business Studies, Psychology, Sociology, Art & Design, Music, Music Technology, Drama & Theatre Studies, Computer Science, Physical Education, and Philosophy & Ethics.

The Extended Project Qualification (EPQ) is offered to all Sixth Form students as an additional standalone qualification. It develops independent research skills and is valued by universities. Approximately 85% of Sixth Form students undertake the EPQ.

GCSE subject choices are made at the end of Year 9. A-Level subject choices are finalised at the end of Year 11, subject to minimum GCSE grade requirements (typically grade 6 or above in the relevant subject).
title: Subjects

text:
The school day runs Monday to Friday. Registration begins at 8:35am. Six timetabled periods of 50 minutes each run from 8:45am to 3:30pm.

Daily structure:
- 8:35am — Registration
- 8:45am — Period 1
- 9:35am — Period 2
- 10:25am — Period 3
- 11:15am — Morning break (20 minutes)
- 11:35am — Period 4
- 12:25pm — Period 5
- 1:15pm — Lunch (45 minutes)
- 2:00pm — Period 6
- 2:50pm — Period 7 (Wednesday and Friday only; other days finish at 2:50pm)
- 3:30pm — End of school day

After-school clubs, activities, and sports fixtures run from 3:30pm to 5:30pm on weekdays. Supervised prep (homework) sessions are available in the library until 5:30pm daily.

Year 12 and 13 students have regular study periods within the timetable. The school does not operate a Saturday school, though select sports fixtures and concerts may take place on Saturday mornings.

The academic year is divided into three terms: Michaelmas (September–December), Lent (January–March), and Summer (April–July), each with a half-term break of one week.
title: Timetable

text:
**Years 7–11:** Dark navy blazer with the Beri College badge, white shirt, school tie in the pupil's house colour, plain grey trousers or grey skirt (knee-length minimum), and plain black leather shoes. A navy V-neck jumper with the school logo may be worn under the blazer in colder months.

**Sixth Form dress code:** Business casual is expected. Smart trousers or skirt, a collared shirt, blouse, or smart top are required. No sportswear, trainers, or casual clothing. Sixth Form students do not wear a blazer or tie.

**PE kit:** Navy polo shirt with the school crest, navy shorts or skorts, plain white socks, and trainers. A navy tracksuit is available for colder weather. All kit must be labelled with the pupil's full name.

Uniform is available from the school's official supplier. A second-hand uniform shop is run by the Parent Association and opens on selected dates each term — details are circulated at the start of each academic year.
title: Uniform

text:
Over 80 clubs and societies run weekly across lunch and after school, covering academic, creative, and recreational interests.

The Duke of Edinburgh's Award is offered at Bronze (Year 9), Silver (Year 10), and Gold (Year 12). Beri College has a 95% completion rate at Gold level.

Programmes include: Model United Nations, debating society, chess club, coding club, film society, drama society, Young Enterprise, and Amnesty International group.

The annual whole-school production takes place each autumn term. The inter-house drama competition is held in the spring term. Both events are staged in the 350-seat Beri Theatre.

The trips programme includes language exchanges with partner schools in France, Germany, and Spain. Year 9 pupils undertake an expedition week in the Lake District. A biennial World Challenge expedition takes Sixth Form students to destinations in South-East Asia or South America.
title: Co-curricular

text:
The Music Department runs three orchestras (Symphony Orchestra, Chamber Orchestra, and String Ensemble), two concert bands, and four choirs including a chamber choir and gospel ensemble.

Individual and small-group tuition is available in over 25 instruments, taught by visiting specialist teachers. Lessons are arranged on a rotating timetable to minimise disruption to academic classes.

The annual Spring Concert is held at Elmbridge Civic Hall and is the flagship event of the music calendar. Additional concerts include the Christmas Carol Service, Lunchtime Recital Series, and House Music Competition.

The purpose-built music school houses a recording studio, twelve practice rooms, and an industry-standard music technology suite used for A-Level Music Technology.

ABRSM and Trinity Guildhall examination preparation is offered to all instrumental pupils. The school regularly achieves Distinction rates above 70% in external music examinations.

A chamber music programme for advanced players runs throughout the year, with regular masterclasses hosted by visiting professional musicians from leading London ensembles.
title: Music

text:
Core sports: rugby, football, cricket, athletics, swimming, netball, tennis, and cross-country. All pupils participate in timetabled games sessions twice per week.

The high-performance programme supports county and national-level athletes, with links to Surrey County Cricket Club, Harlequins Rugby Academy, and Swim England South East regional programme.

Facilities include: a modern sports hall, 25-metre six-lane indoor swimming pool, fully equipped gymnasium, fitness suite, and 14 acres of playing fields with dedicated rugby, football, and cricket pitches.

Recent honours: Surrey U15 Rugby Champions 2024; National Schools Swimming Championships finalist 2024; Surrey Girls Netball Cup winners 2024; ESSA Team Swimming relay gold 2024.

Partnerships with Elmbridge FC, Surrey Cricket Board, and Swim England South East provide additional coaching, fixture opportunities, and talent identification pathways for pupils.
title: Sport

text:
Beri College is a fictitious independent co-educational day school for pupils aged 11–18, used to demonstrate BERI Labs' AI education framework. It is modelled on a selective independent school in Elmbridge, Surrey, with approximately 900 pupils across Years 7–13.

The school's ethos centres on academic rigour, personal development, and service to the community. It aims to develop curious, confident, and compassionate young people prepared for life beyond school.

Beri College is a member of the Headmasters' and Headmistresses' Conference (HMC) and the Independent Schools Council (ISC). It holds ISI inspection ratings of Excellent across all categories.

The school operates a house system, an extensive co-curricular programme, and strong links with the local community.
title: School Overview

text:
**Headmaster:** Mr Jonathan Fairfax MA (Oxon) joined Beri College in 2019, previously serving as Deputy Head at a leading HMC school in the South East.

**Deputy Head (Academic):** Dr Sarah Mwangi PhD, oversees curriculum, timetabling, and academic standards.

**Deputy Head (Pastoral):** Mr David Okafor, responsible for pupil wellbeing, the house system, and behaviour policy.

**Head of Sixth Form:** Ms Priya Sharma, leads Sixth Form provision including UCAS guidance and enrichment.

**Bursar:** Mrs Helen Cartwright, manages finance, estates, and operations.

**Head of Admissions:** Mrs Laura Chen handles all enquiries and open events. Contact: admissions@bericollege.example.com or 01372 000 000.

The Senior Leadership Team meets weekly and is supported by a Board of Governors comprising independent professionals, parents, and community representatives.
title: Leadership

text:
Beri College operates a four-house system. Every pupil is assigned to a house on entry and remains in it throughout their time at school. The four houses are:

- **Ashton** (red) — named after a pioneer in education
- **Bramley** (blue) — named after a local historical figure
- **Croft** (green) — named after a distinguished alumna
- **Devere** (gold) — named after a school founder

Each house is led by a Head of House (staff) and elected Sixth Form prefects. Inter-house competitions include House Music, House Drama, House Sports Day, House Quiz, and a Lent-term charity challenge. The House Cup is awarded at the end of the Summer term. House ties worn by Years 7–11 display the pupil's house colour.
title: Houses

text:
Every pupil has a Form Tutor who monitors academic progress, wellbeing, and attendance and meets with their tutor group each morning. Tutors are the first point of contact for parents with pastoral concerns.

The school employs a full-time School Counsellor and a qualified Mental Health Lead. A visiting Educational Psychologist attends half-termly. Drop-in wellbeing sessions are available on Tuesdays and Thursdays at lunchtime.

An Anti-Bullying Ambassador programme is run by trained Year 10 and 12 pupils. PSHE is timetabled for all year groups, covering mental health, relationships, online safety, financial literacy, and careers. Sixth Form pupils have access to a dedicated counsellor and a Peer Mentoring scheme.
title: Pastoral Care

text:
Beri College runs school coaches serving Esher, Cobham, Weybridge, Walton-on-Thames, Guildford, and Kingston upon Thames. Timetables are published at the start of each academic year.

The nearest railway station is Elmbridge Central (8-minute walk). Trains run from London Waterloo (approx. 35 minutes) and Guildford (approx. 20 minutes).

Secure, covered cycle storage is available on site. On-site parking is limited and reserved for staff. A drop-off zone on Beri Lane operates 7:50–8:30am and 3:30–4:00pm.

text:
Lunch is included in the termly fee and served in the main dining hall. A hot meal, vegetarian option, salad bar, and soup are provided daily. Menus are planned by a nutritionist on a three-week rotation.

The school is fully nut-aware. Pupils with allergies or dietary requirements (halal, vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free) register needs with the School Office. The Beri Pantry café is open from 7:45am and at morning break, serving hot drinks and snacks. Sixth Form students may use it during free periods. Energy drinks are not permitted on site.
title: Food and Catering

text:
The school library holds over 18,000 volumes and is open 8:00am–6:00pm. A qualified Librarian manages the collection and supports research skills. Years 7–9 have a fortnightly timetabled library lesson.

Online databases include JSTOR, Encyclopaedia Britannica, and a school e-book platform. The library hosts a Book Club, author visits, and the annual Beri Book Prize. Sixth Form students may reserve private silent-study desks. A careers library is located adjacent to the main library.
title: Library and Resources

text:
All classrooms have interactive displays and high-speed Wi-Fi. Years 7–11 are encouraged to bring a personal device; a loan scheme exists for those who need one. Sixth Form students have access to a 1:1 school-managed laptop scheme.

A 40-workstation computer suite is available for lessons and free study. The school uses Google Workspace for Education and hosts learning materials on its VLE. The IT helpdesk operates 8:00am–5:00pm daily. Acceptable Use Policies are signed annually by pupils and parents.
title: Technology and IT
